doc.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 23, 2003 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Touring with Benny Goodman in 1970 and his sense of tempo
summary: Six weeks away with Goodman, whom he loved as a teacher and father figure, and watching his foot for tempo.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: But then I went away with Benny Goodman in 1970, I went away for six weeks, with Ruth. I thought it was important to go with him because I always wanted to play with him. I had done a few gigs with him at the Waldorf, but this was a serious gig and I said let’s do it. So Ruth’s mother took care of the kids, sent them off to school. And all I had to do was leave in the morning and come back, and then six weeks later we were home and that was —
Yeah. Well you seem to have a great relationship with him for, what almost twenty years?

Oh Benny was the king, the king. I loved Benny Goodman. He was a teacher, he was almost like a father to me. We discussed a lot of things and we knew where each — I knew where he was and he knew where I was. And we always had a good time.

Yeah. I told you, I said he never — he rarely counted off. He would start the number and that was the tempo you had to pick — know where that second beat was. See? And I was so close to him, I’d watch his foot all the time, so I knew exactly where he was.
It’s good that he was one of those people that tapped the way they are playing.
Yeah. He was a little on top of it, but you knew where he was. Yeah.
